crisis.detail: Jul 29: US pauses Iran strikes for 5th consecutive day - US-Iran de-escalation pause extends to day 5 (Jul 25-29) with continued Omani mediation in Tehran (CBS/AP, Jul 27-29); Iran denies direct talks but confirms Omani dialogue on Hormuz passage mechanisms; Saudi intercepts drones targeting oil facilities launched from Iraq (France 24/AFP, Jul 27); Houthis claim attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Jizan/Yanbu (NHK, Jul 27); Brent $86.81, down 13.78% from intraday peak (Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 29); 78 vessels through Hormuz since Saturday; tail 40%

commodityScenario: Jul 29: US-Iran strike pause extends to a 5th consecutive day (Jul 25-29) — the longest break since hostilities began. Iran confirms Omani-led talks on Hormuz passage mechanisms continue in Tehran; no direct US-Iran negotiations. Saudi Arabia intercepted Iraq-launched drones targeting petroleum facilities for a second straight day (France 24/AFP, Jul 27); Houthis continue to claim Red Sea attacks. Brent was $86.81, down 13.78% from intraday peak (Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 29), as markets priced further diplomatic progress. TTF eased to 56.50 EUR/MWh, down 8.72% from Jul 27 levels (Yahoo Finance TTF=F). CNN reported 78 vessels transited Hormuz since Saturday, citing Marisks; the count is not LNG-specific. Tail remains at 40% as pause continues but drone/missile attacks on Saudi infrastructure keep escalation risk elevated.

todaysEvents.delta: Neutral: The US-Iran pause extended through Jul 29 for a fifth consecutive day. Iran confirmed continued Omani mediation in Tehran but denied direct US talks. No Hormuz framework has been announced. Sources: CBS/AP, CNN.

Up: Saudi Arabia intercepted Iraq-launched drones targeting petroleum facilities and Riyadh for a second consecutive day. Houthis separately claimed attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure at Yanbu and Jizan, sustaining Red Sea route risk. Sources: France 24/AFP, Jul 27; NHK, Jul 27.

Down: Brent was $86.81, down 13.78% from its intraday peak (Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 29), as the pause and Omani talks further reduced the risk premium. TTF eased to 56.50 EUR/MWh as European gas priced de-escalation.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: The Omani-led diplomatic channel gains further traction as the mutual pause extends past 4 days. Iran-US indirect talks via Oman produce a framework for phased Hormuz reopening and restoration of the June MOU ceasefire. Brent settles toward $75-85/bbl as risk premium deflates materially. Probability raised to 25% reflecting extended pause, constructive Omani dialogue, and Trump's public engagement signal.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Pause collapses after talks fail to make progress on core issues (Hormuz control, nuclear program, blockade conditions). US resumes intermittent strikes; Iran retaliates at a constrained tempo. Hormuz remains constrained with limited tanker transits. Brent trades $80-100/bbl, TTF stays elevated. Probability unchanged at 35% given hawkish rhetoric from both sides and ongoing drone/missile activity against Saudi.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Diplomacy fails outright and the pause breaks down. US strikes resume at scale, potentially targeting nuclear sites. Iran escalates with full-scale offensive ops. Kuwait water infrastructure already damaged; GCC states face sustained attacks. Brent spikes $100-130+/bbl, JKM above $30/MMBtu. Probability reduced from 45% to 40% reflecting the extended pause and positive Omani diplomatic signals, but still elevated given unresolved conflict drivers.
